unit.title: Cells: The Building Blocks of Life

lesson.title: Review: Cells, the Building Blocks of Life
lesson.subject: science

contentBlocks.text: This week you zoomed from a single cell all the way up to whole organ systems. Let's put it all together.

Quick review: all living things are made of one or more cells (Day 1). A cell's parts — nucleus, cell membrane, cytoplasm, mitochondria — each have a specific job (Day 2). Plant cells have a cell wall and chloroplasts that animal cells don't (Day 3). Cells organize into tissues, organs, and organ systems (Day 4). Draw one complete diagram tracing all four ideas: a labeled cell, noting whether it's plant or animal, and how it fits into the larger tissue-organ-system hierarchy.
Great work investigating cells this week! You now understand the basic unit of life and how it builds up into the complex systems that keep every living thing alive.

objectives: Recall and correctly apply all four cell concepts from the week: cell theory, cell parts, plant/animal differences, and organizational hierarchy
Create one integrated diagram showing all four ideas together
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child create the integrated diagram combining all 4 ideas.
3. Complete the cumulative review worksheet, mixing all 4 days' concepts.
4. Discuss any mismatches or uncertain answers together before finishing.
5. Celebrate finishing the first full week of investigation — this pattern (5 days building to a review) is how every unit this year will work.
differentiationTips: Struggling: allow the child to use their Day 1-4 worksheets and diagrams as a reference during review rather than working from memory alone
Ready for more: ask them to explain WHY each cell structure exists, connecting form to function, not just naming parts
This is a good checkpoint to note which day's concept needs the most re-teaching before moving to next week's unit
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. All living things are made of one or more cells. 2. The nucleus is the control center, holding genetic instructions. 3. A cell wall and chloroplasts are unique to plant cells. 4. The hierarchy is cell -> tissue -> organ -> organ system.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates NGSS MS-LS1-1 through MS-LS1-3 (cell theory, cell structure/function, and body organization) before the unit moves on, matching the 'consolidate before adding more' pacing established in earlier units this session.

worksheet.title: Cells: The Building Blocks of Life — Week 1 Review

rows.problem: What does the cell theory state?
What is the job of the nucleus?
Name two structures unique to plant cells.
List the organizational hierarchy from cell to organ system.
